authorship: The Alpha Readiness Level (ARL) was devised by Rostyslav Shcherbyna, author of Monte-Neo; it is modelled on the idea of a technology readiness level and is a Monte-Neo scale, not an industry standard.

levels.name: The backtest is not broken
levels.how: monte-neo verify --strategy (probes need code), or alpha with --membership

levels.name: The signal predicts
levels.how: monte-neo alpha (scores), or verify (timing test); Deflated Sharpe of the certificate at least 0.8

levels.name: Tradable and robust
levels.how: alpha with --aum (robustness runs by default), or verify with volume data

levels.name: Confirmed live
levels.how: monte-neo monitor --live live.csv --source real_fills --fills fills.csv (paper and testnet stop at 8)

ceilings.why: the universe may be today's survivors: declare the delisted names (delisted=...) or add their prices

blockers.why: the return is not shown to be more than benchmark exposure
the result rests on a few assets: it does not hold on random subsets of the universe
the result does not survive small noise in the inputs: it fits exact values
the short side could not be borrowed or traded at the size shown
the return is explained by the existing book: it is not new alpha for that book
the signal uses closes of markets that close later than the trade (same date, different time zone)
the edge disappears after its discovery date
the claimed numbers are better than the verified ones
the universe looks like today's members (no name added or delisted): pass a point-in-time membership file (--membership); a fixed universe declares every symbol for the whole period

non_real_sources.why: paper, testnet and simulated fills are not live

criteria.name: Margin
criteria.text: the level's main check passes by a clear margin, not at the threshold

criteria.name: Breadth
criteria.text: the result repeats across independent slices (periods, assets, regimes, start dates)

criteria.name: Sample
criteria.text: enough independent observations for the claim at this level

criteria.name: Out of sample
criteria.text: the same level holds on data that did not choose the parameters (sealed holdout or forward data)

honesty: Thresholds are fixed and versioned before use (arl-rules/2); a change bumps the version, and a certificate records the version it was computed with. The numbers are provisional proposals until calibrated on the Trap Suite and the wild corpus (docs/guides/alpha-calibration.md); arl-rules/2 is frozen only by the owner's decision.
The sealed holdout opens once. If it is opened more than once for the same strategy, D4 is 0 for every level, permanently, and the ledger shows why.
Trials are paid. Depth at levels 4-6 is computed with the full n_trials of the project, not of one idea.
Paper, testnet and simulated fills are not live. They cap ARL at 8; ARL 9 and D4 of level 9 require real fills and a custody statement.
No evidence, no points. 'Not assessed' is shown next to the missing run (--aum, --book, --n-trials, monitor --live).
A depth never lifts the level: ARL 6 depth 4 is still below ARL 7 depth 0.
ARL is not a recommendation to trade and says nothing about future returns.

derived.why: Calibration (350 000 synthetic cases, 2026-11): without it, noise best-of-100 reached level 4 in 78 % of cases; with Deflated Sharpe >= 0.8 at level 4 it reaches it in under 1 %.
derived.next_action: Report every variant tried (--n-trials or a trial ledger) and verify on more data: the Sharpe does not survive the number of variants tried.

changes: arl-rules/2 (from arl-rules/1): level 4 also needs selection_adjusted_sharpe (Deflated Sharpe of the certificate >= 0.8, computed with at least the project's number of trials).

arl-rules/2: level 5 is also blocked when one of these checks ran and warned or failed: universe_subsampling, noise_injection, short_feasibility, residual_vs_book, cross_market_close_alignment, post_discovery_decay, claim_consistency. Calibration (350 000 cases): cross-sectional traps at level 5 or above 39 % -> 8 %, planted edge 65 % -> 59 %.

arl-rules/2: level 5 is blocked when universe_lookahead warns (a cross-section whose universe looks like today's members). A point-in-time membership file lifts it; for a fixed universe (FX, futures) the file lists every symbol for the whole period.
